findings.title: trim_and_pad silently SCRAMBLES row (observation/time) order for any non-RangeIndex index
findings.description: hypertools/align/common.py trim_and_pad() computes the common rows across datasets with Python sets: `rows = set(data[0].index.values)`, intersects, then `rows = list(rows)` (line ~41) and reindexes every dataset with `d.loc[rows]`. `list(set(...))` iterates in hash-bucket order, so the output rows come out in an ARBITRARY order for any index that is not a contiguous small-integer RangeIndex. Strings, pandas DatetimeIndex (the flagship fMRI/timeseries use case), and non-contiguous/shuffled integer indices are ALL scrambled. Because hyp.align returns bare numpy arrays (via _to_arrays, no index), the reordering is completely silent and unrecoverable by the caller. Alignment across datasets stays internally consistent (all datasets share the same reordered `rows` list, so output row j maps to the same original observation in every dataset), so numeric dispersion/quality metrics still look fine -- but the returned data no longer corresponds row-for-row to the input, and any trajectory/timeseries plotted from it is garbage. Default RangeIndex 0..n-1 happens to survive (small-int set order == sorted), which is why unit tests and the gallery (all integer-indexed) never caught it. Root cause + fix validated in scratch: replacing line 41 with an order-preserving intersection `rows = [r for r in data[0].index.values if r in rows]` restores input order exactly. This affects HyperAlign, Procrustes, all SRM variants, and NullAlign (every path goes through trim_and_pad in both fit and transform).
findings.repro:
import warnings, numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
n,k=10,3
base=np.zeros((n,k)); base[:,0]=np.arange(n)   # row i is identifiable: col0==i
tidx=pd.date_range('2020-01-01', periods=n, freq='s')
d0=pd.DataFrame(base, index=tidx); d1=pd.DataFrame(base.copy(), index=tidx)
with warnings.catch_warnings():
    warnings.simplefilter('ignore')
    out=hyp.align([d0,d1], model='NullAlign')  # NullAlign: no math, pure trim_and_pad order
print(list(np.asarray(out[0])[:,0].astype(int)))  # expect 0..9
findings.actual: [7, 4, 5, 0, 2, 6, 1, 3, 9, 8]  (public hyp.align, DatetimeIndex). Also: string idx t00..t11 -> ['t06','t10','t00','t07','t01','t05','t02','t04','t03','t08','t11','t09']; DatetimeIndex ORDER PRESERVED=False; RangeIndex 0..n-1 -> preserved (bug hides).

findings.title: SRM/DetSRM/RSRM `features` default documented as 'minimum number of columns' but is actually the MAX (padded common width)
findings.description: SharedResponseModel/DeterministicSharedResponseModel/RobustSharedResponseModel docstrings (hypertools/align/srm.py) say `features` defaults to 'minimum number of columns across datasets'. But Aligner.fit runs trim_and_pad FIRST, which zero-pads every dataset to the MAX column count; srm.py fitter then computes `features = np.min([d.shape[1] for d in data])` over the already-padded (all-equal) widths, yielding the MAX of the original column counts, not the min. For datasets with 6/4/8 columns the doc predicts 4 but the actual default is 8. Equal-width inputs are unaffected (min==max). Either the docstring should say 'the common (zero-padded) column count, i.e. the maximum number of columns across datasets' or the default should be computed on pre-pad widths.
findings.repro:
import warnings, numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
ds=[np.random.randn(30,6), np.random.randn(30,4), np.random.randn(30,8)]
with warnings.catch_warnings():
    warnings.simplefilter('ignore')
    out,m=hyp.align(ds, model='SRM', return_model=True)
print('features=',m.features,'out cols=',np.asarray(out[0]).shape[1])

findings.title: Data-loss ('keeps only N rows') warning is emitted twice for a single hyp.align() call
findings.description: trim_and_pad emits the 'alignment keeps only the N row(s) common to all datasets' UserWarning. A single hyp.align() runs fit_transform = fit() + transform(), and BOTH call trim_and_pad, so the identical warning fires twice per call (and would fire once more per extra transform on the reused model). Noisy and can mislead users into thinking two separate trims happened. Emit once (e.g. only in fit, or dedupe).
findings.repro:
import warnings, numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
ds=[np.random.randn(40,5), np.random.randn(30,5)]
with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:
    warnings.simplefilter('always')
    hyp.align(ds, model='NullAlign')
print(sum('keeps only' in str(x.message) for x in w))

findings.title: hyp.align(single non-list array) returns a list-of-one, inconsistent with hyp.reduce (bare array) and its own docstring
findings.description: align()'s Returns docstring says output is 'in the same list/single-item shape as data (matching hyp.reduce/hyp.cluster/hyp.manip...)'. But hyp.align(bare_array) returns a Python list containing one array, whereas hyp.reduce(bare_array) returns a bare ndarray. So align does NOT match reduce's single-item convention as claimed. The Aligner transformer always builds a list comprehension, so single (non-list) input is up-promoted to list-of-one and _to_arrays keeps it a list.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
X=np.random.randn(30,5)
print(type(hyp.align(X, model='NullAlign')).__name__, '<- align')
print(type(hyp.reduce(X, reduce={'model':'PCA','args':[],'kwargs':{'n_components':3}})).__name__, '<- reduce')
findings.expected: align single-array -> bare ndarray (to match reduce and the docstring)
findings.actual: align(single array) -> list[len1]; reduce(single array)-> ndarray shape(30,3)

findings.title: Aligner classes (HyperAlign, Procrustes, SRM...) are not importable via hypertools.align.* nor exposed at top level, though the docstring says you may pass an instance
findings.description: align()'s docstring says model= may be 'a bare (uninstantiated) Aligner subclass, an already-constructed instance'. But the top-level `from .align.align import align` in hypertools/__init__.py REBINDS the name `hypertools.align` to the function, shadowing the subpackage: `import hypertools.align as A` yields the function, and hypertools.align.HyperAlign / hyp.HyperAlign do not exist. To construct an instance a user must know the deep private path e.g. `from hypertools.align.hyperalign import HyperAlign` / `hypertools.align.procrustes.Procrustes`. Expose the aligner classes (top-level, or on the function object, or document the import paths) so the documented instance/subclass spec form is actually usable.
findings.repro:
import hypertools as hyp
print(type(hyp.align).__name__)          # function
import hypertools.align as A
print(type(A).__name__)                  # function (subpackage shadowed)
print(hasattr(hyp,'HyperAlign'))         # False
findings.expected: a discoverable public path to HyperAlign/Procrustes/SharedResponseModel/... classes
findings.actual: hyp.align is a function; `import hypertools.align as A` -> function; hasattr(hyp,'HyperAlign') False

findings.title: hyp.align([]) (empty list) loads the minipedia text corpus and dies with a cryptic LatentDirichletAllocation error
findings.description: Passing an empty list to hyp.align falls through to format_data, which treats it as text input: it prints 'loading corpus: minipedia...' (a surprising side effect / network+disk load for an empty input) and then raises 'ValueError: Found array with 0 sample(s) (shape=(0, 1220)) while a minimum of 1 is required by LatentDirichletAllocation'. Aligner.fit already has `assert data is not None, ValueError('cannot align empty dataset')` but an empty LIST is not None so it never guards. align() should reject an empty dataset list up front with a clear message.
findings.repro:
import hypertools as hyp
hyp.align([], model='HyperAlign')
findings.expected: clear error e.g. 'cannot align an empty list of datasets'
findings.actual: loading corpus: minipedia...done!  ValueError: Found array with 0 sample(s) (shape=(0, 1220)) while a minimum of 1 is required by LatentDirichletAllocation.

findings.title: HyperAlign n_iter validation uses assert (stripped under python -O); float n_iter silently truncated
findings.description: HyperAlign.__init__ validates with `assert n_iter >= 0, 'n_iter must be non-negative'`. asserts are removed when Python runs with -O, so validation silently disappears in optimized deployments; a negative n_iter would then reach `max(1, int(n_iter))` and run 1 pass instead of erroring. Raise ValueError instead. Separately, a non-integer n_iter (e.g. 2.5) is accepted and silently truncated by int(); consider rejecting or documenting the truncation.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
ds=[np.random.randn(20,4) for _ in range(3)]
hyp.align(ds, model='HyperAlign', n_iter=-1)   # AssertionError, not ValueError
hyp.align(ds, model='HyperAlign', n_iter=2.5)  # runs, int()->2 silently
findings.expected: ValueError('n_iter must be a non-negative integer') robust under -O
findings.actual: AssertionError: n_iter must be non-negative ; n_iter=2.5 runs with silent truncation

findings.title: Procrustes error messages: giant embedded whitespace + jargony 'invariant in time datasets'
findings.description: hypertools/align/procrustes.py builds error strings with backslash line-continuations inside the string literal, so the raised message contains long runs of spaces: 'reduction=False, so mapping from                               higher dimensionality                               template space is not supported. template space had 8 while target 3 dimensions'. Also, an all-zero/near-constant dataset raises 'For now do not handle invariant in time datasets' -- ungrammatical and leaks dev-note phrasing; it should read e.g. 'cannot align a dataset with zero variance (a constant/invariant column)'. Clean up the whitespace and wording.

hyp.align([np.zeros((20,4)), np.random.randn(20,4)], model='Procrustes')

findings.title: Datasets with zero index overlap yield silent empty (0, k) arrays
findings.description: When aligned datasets share NO index values, trim_and_pad's intersection is empty and hyp.align returns empty (0, k) arrays. Only the generic 'keeps only the 0 row(s) common' warning is emitted (easily missed / suppressed). Producing empty output for a fit is a strong signal the user mismatched their data; consider raising a clear error ('datasets share no common observations to align') rather than returning empty arrays.
findings.repro:
import warnings, numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
a=pd.DataFrame(np.random.randn(4,4), index=[0,1,2,3])
b=pd.DataFrame(np.random.randn(4,4), index=[10,11,12,13])
with warnings.catch_warnings():
    warnings.simplefilter('ignore')
    print([np.asarray(o).shape for o in hyp.align([a,b], model='HyperAlign')])
findings.expected: clear error about no common observations

findings.title: [infra] .venv ships a STALE non-editable hypertools that lacks release-branch fixes
findings.description: The audit .venv's site-packages contains a NON-editable copy of hypertools (/Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/hypertools) that predates branch audit/release-1.0-2026-07: it lacks the _reject_unknown_aligner guard, so hyp.align(data, model='Nope') on that copy raises the cryptic "AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'fit_transform'" instead of the clear ValueError present in the repo source. A script imported from outside the repo picks up the stale copy (sys.path[0] = script dir), while a `-c` run from the repo root picks up the source. This is an environment/packaging issue (not an align code bug on the release branch), but it will silently make anyone's `pip`-installed hypertools diverge from the release; the package should be reinstalled (`pip install -e .`) before release and CI should assert import path.
